description: Simulation to teach integrated business management through a coworking space startup in Santiago, Chile. Students make cross-functional decisions across marketing, operations, finance, and strategy over 3 rounds, observing how each decision affects financial performance, customer satisfaction, and competitive position simultaneously. Grounded in the Business Model Canvas, Balanced Scorecard, Value Chain, STP, and organizational structure frameworks.

howtoplay:
# How to Play — El Negocio Completo (Nexo Coworking)

You are the General Manager of Nexo Coworking, a Santiago coworking space that just finished a thin-but-profitable first year (61% occupancy, +CLP $600K/mo EBITDA). Over **3 rounds** (each = 6 months) you steer four functions at once and watch them interact.

**Each round, set six decisions:**
1. **Target Segment** — freelancers, corporate, startups, or students. Each has a different willingness-to-pay, churn, and facility preference.
2. **Monthly Price** (CLP 60–140K) — price above a segment's willingness-to-pay loses demand; pricing below it lifts demand but thins margin.
3. **Facilities Focus** — match it to what your segment values (e.g. corporate → private spaces).
4. **Service Level** — basic / standard / premium. Charging premium prices with a basic service triggers bad reviews.
5. **Staffing (+ training)** — enables service quality and lowers churn.
6. **Strategic Initiative** — referral, university partnership, quality certification, virtual membership, or a pop-up second location.

In Rounds 2 and 3 you also answer an **event**: a lease-renewal choice (R2) and an anchor-tenant offer (R3).

**Watch four Balanced-Scorecard quadrants** (Financial, Customer, Internal Process, Learning & Growth), your **cash balance**, and your **Model Coherence** score (0–20). You are graded /100 on EBITDA margin, occupancy, NPS, coherence, and churn. The winning play is a *coherent* one — decisions that reinforce each other — not the highest price or fullest room. Use **Undo Last Round** to revisit a decision. A full debrief with your income statement and a before/after Business Model Canvas appears at the end.
teachingnote:
# Teaching Note — Sim 290 "El Negocio Completo" (Business & Strategy Primer)

**Level:** Introductory (first-year / non-majors). **Duration:** 75 min, 3 rounds (6 months each). **Frameworks:** Business Model Canvas (Osterwalder & Pigneur), Porter Value Chain, Balanced Scorecard (Kaplan & Norton), STP (Kotler), Mintzberg structures.

## Learning objectives
- **LO1** Business-model architecture (complete a simplified BMC for Nexo).
- **LO2** Functional interdependence (trace cause–effect chains across marketing/operations/finance).
- **LO3** Basic financial literacy (read the income statement; is the business improving or deteriorating?).
- **LO4** Competitive positioning (differentiate vs WeXpand, Espacio Libre, Nodo Creativo).
- **LO5** Stakeholder trade-offs (members, employees, investors).
- **LO6** Strategy as pattern (coherent choices vs ad-hoc reactions).

## The core teaching mechanism
Every decision has a cross-functional consequence: lower price → higher occupancy → higher cost-to-serve → thinner margin → strategic review before competitors react. The **Model Coherence** score (four pairwise checks: segment↔price, segment↔facilities, price↔service, initiative↔segment; 0–5 each, max 20) rewards internal consistency over maximizing any single metric.

## What good and poor play look like (verified against the model)
- **Coherent corporate** (price ~115 within WTP, private facilities, premium service + manager, certification): grows toward full occupancy, positive EBITDA, high NPS — top band.
- **Lowball / mismatched** (deep discount or wrong facility for the segment): fills desks but thin margin + high churn → negative EBITDA, cash falls. Teaches that occupancy is a vanity headline.
- **Premium price + basic service**: triggers a viral negative review (NPS −12). Teaches price↔service coherence.
- **Constant segment pivoting**: acquisition penalty + churn spike. Teaches strategy-as-pattern (LO6).

## Three natural pause points
Pause 1 (after R1): occupancy vs margin trade-off. Pause 2 (after R2): leading indicators — did an R2 NPS/churn signal predict an R3 revenue move? Pause 3 (after R3): full debrief.

## Debrief protocol (ORID) — Spanish prompts
**Objective:** "¿Cuál fue tu EBITDA final vs Round 1? ¿NPS y churn final? ¿Cuántos bloques del Canvas cambiaron?"
**Reflective:** "¿Cuál ronda fue la más difícil? ¿Cuándo sentiste que el negocio 'corría solo'? ¿Mayor presión: competidores o fuga de clientes?"
**Interpretive:** "¿Por qué los modelos más coherentes rindieron mejor aunque no tuvieran el precio ni la ocupación más altos? ¿Relación NPS → resultados financieros futuros? ¿Puede ser sostenible un negocio que hace felices a los clientes pero no gana dinero?"
**Decisional:** "Si lanzaras Nexo mañana, ¿qué decisión cambiarías primero? ¿Cómo aplica la 'coherencia del modelo' a una decisión personal como elegir carrera?"

## Assessment options
A) Auto-graded sim score (5 KPIs, ~10% of grade). B) BMC evolution (1 page). C) GM memo to investors (400 words, ≥3 financial + 2 non-financial metrics). D) Stakeholder impact analysis (groups, 500 words).

## Performance bands
85–100 Emprendedor Estratégico · 70–84 Gestor Competente · 55–69 En Transición · <55 Negocio en Riesgo.
casestudy:
# El Negocio Completo — GM's Desk at Nexo Coworking (STR-2026-290)

**Setting:** Santiago, Chile. Nexo Coworking S.R.L. — one facility in Barrio Italia/Providencia, 48 workstations (40 hot desks, 8 dedicated), ~58 members, 61% occupancy of workstation-hours, CLP $5.8M monthly revenue against CLP $5.2M cost (a thin but positive CLP $600K EBITDA, 10.3% margin). **Protagonist:** Francisca Aránguiz-Pino, 36, General Manager.

**The situation.** Year 1 proved the concept by doing one thing: fill the space and pay the rent. Year 2 is different — it is an *integrated* operation where four levers interact and cannot be pulled in isolation. The board has asked Francisca to commit to a three-period (18-month) pattern rather than react quarter to quarter.

**The market.** Nexo sits between international operators (WeXpand Chile, Las Condes, CLP $130K/desk — about to cut to $105K) and low-cost local players (Espacio Libre, Barrio Lastarria, CLP $72K; Nodo Creativo, Vitacura, CLP $105K, design-led, high NPS), plus informal competition from cafés installing fiber and bookable desks. Four member segments pull in different directions: freelancers (volume, price-sensitive, high churn), corporate remote workers (margin, low churn, want private rooms and a professional address), startups (growth, medium sensitivity), and students (very price-sensitive, semester churn).

**The tension the case surfaces.** Dropping price to chase occupancy cascades — more members strain Wi-Fi and concierge time, cost-to-serve rises, and gross margin falls a period later. Investing only in sales stalls member experience; investing only in facilities stalls acquisition. Customer-satisfaction (a leading indicator) in one round predicts revenue retention in the next. And promising a value proposition the resources can't deliver — targeting corporate without private rooms or upgraded service — creates a Business-Model-Canvas inconsistency that the scorecard penalizes.

**Round 2:** WeXpand's price cut lands, and the landlord offers a 3-year lease (+15% rent, stability) or a 1-year renewal (flexibility). **Round 3:** a major tech firm offers to place 15 remote workers in dedicated desks for 12 months — an anchor tenant that expands capacity and revenue but needs investment in private space — just as neighborhood word-of-mouth swings.

**The decision.** Across three six-month periods Francisca must set segment, price, facilities focus, service level, staffing, and one strategic initiative — and be judged not on the occupancy headline but on whether the pattern of choices is *coherent*: a strategy, not a series of reactions.
